title: 10. NLP, Transformers & LLMs: Modern NLP Models: BERT, GPT, and T5 Families
summary: Covers The Three Families, BERT: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers, BERT Variants, GPT: Generative Pre-trained Transformer, GPT Variants & Open-Source Alternatives and more.
objectives: BERT: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers

sections.title: The Three Families
sections.body:
**Goal**: Master the major model families powering modern NLP.

```
BERT Family (Encoder-only)
├─ BERT, RoBERTa, DistilBERT, ALBERT
└─ Use: Understanding tasks (classification, NER, QA)

GPT Family (Decoder-only)
├─ GPT-2, GPT-3, GPT-4, LLaMA, Mistral
└─ Use: Generation tasks (text generation, chat, completion)

T5 Family (Encoder-Decoder)
├─ T5, FLAN-T5, BART, mT5
└─ Use: Transformation tasks (translation, summarization, QA)
```

sections.title: BERT: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers
sections.body:
### Architecture: Encoder-only

```
Input: "The [MASK] sat on the mat"
       ↓
   ┌────────────┐
   │  Embedding │
   └────────────┘
       ↓
   ┌────────────┐
   │ Transformer│
   │  Encoder   │  × 12 layers (base)
   │ (Bidir.)   │  × 24 layers (large)
   └────────────┘
       ↓
   Contextualized
   Representations

Output: Predict [MASK] = "cat"
```

### Pre-training Tasks:

**1. Masked Language Modeling (MLM)**
```
Original: "The cat sat on the mat"
Masked:   "The [MASK] sat on the [MASK]"
Task:     Predict masked words

• Masks 15% of tokens
• Forces model to use bidirectional context
```

**2. Next Sentence Prediction (NSP)**
```
Sentence A: "The cat sat on the mat"
Sentence B: "It was sleeping"

Task: IsNext? (True/False)

• 50% actual next sentences
• 50% random sentences
• Learns sentence relationships
```

### Special Tokens:
```
[CLS]: Classification token (start of sequence)
[SEP]: Separator between sentences
[MASK]: Masked token for MLM
[PAD]: Padding token
```

### Model Sizes:

```
BERT-base:
  • Layers: 12
  • Hidden: 768
  • Heads: 12
  • Parameters: 110M

BERT-large:
  • Layers: 24
  • Hidden: 1024
  • Heads: 16
  • Parameters: 340M
```

### When to Use BERT:
```
✓ Text classification (sentiment, topic)
✓ Named Entity Recognition (NER)
✓ Question Answering (extractive)
✓ Sentence similarity
✓ Token classification
✗ Text generation (not designed for it!)
```

sections.title: BERT Variants
sections.body:
### 1. RoBERTa (Robustly Optimized BERT)
```
Improvements over BERT:
✓ Remove NSP task (not helpful)
✓ Train longer (500K steps vs 1M)
✓ Larger batches
✓ More data
✓ Dynamic masking

Result: +2-3% performance gain
```

### 2. DistilBERT
```
Idea: Distill BERT knowledge into smaller model

Process:
  Teacher (BERT) → Student (DistilBERT)
  Copy soft predictions

Results:
✓ 40% smaller (66M params)
✓ 60% faster
✓ Retains 97% performance

Use: Production deployment (speed matters)
```

### 3. ALBERT (A Lite BERT)
```
Innovations:
✓ Factorized embeddings (smaller embedding matrix)
✓ Cross-layer parameter sharing (same weights across layers)
✓ Sentence Order Prediction (SOP) instead of NSP

Results:
✓ 18× fewer parameters than BERT-large
✓ Similar or better performance

Use: Resource-constrained environments
```

sections.title: GPT: Generative Pre-trained Transformer
sections.body:
### Architecture: Decoder-only (causal/masked attention)

```
Input: "The cat sat"
       ↓
   ┌────────────┐
   │  Embedding │
   └────────────┘
       ↓
   ┌────────────┐
   │ Transformer│
   │  Decoder   │  × 12-96+ layers
   │ (Causal)   │  (masked attention)
   └────────────┘
       ↓
   Probability
   Distribution

Output: Predict next word → "on"
```

### Pre-training Task: **Language Modeling**

```
Input:  "The cat sat"
Target: "cat sat on"  (shifted by 1)

Task: Predict next token given previous tokens

• Autoregressive (left-to-right)
• No masking needed
• Simple but effective!
```

### GPT Evolution:

```
GPT-1 (2018):
  • Layers: 12
  • Hidden: 768
  • Parameters: 117M
  • Training: BooksCorpus

GPT-2 (2019):
  • Layers: 48 (large)
  • Hidden: 1600
  • Parameters: 1.5B (large)
  • Training: WebText (40GB)
  • "Too dangerous to release" (initially)

GPT-3 (2020):
  • Layers: 96
  • Hidden: 12288
  • Parameters: 175B
  • Training: 300B tokens
  • Few-shot learning capability!

GPT-4 (2023):
  • Parameters: Unknown (rumored 1.76T)
  • Multimodal (text + images)
  • Significantly better reasoning
```

### When to Use GPT:
```
✓ Text generation
✓ Creative writing
✓ Code generation
✓ Completion tasks
✓ Chat/dialogue
✓ Few-shot learning
```

sections.title: GPT Variants & Open-Source Alternatives
sections.body:
### 1. GPT-2 (Open-source)
```python
from transformers import GPT2LMHeadModel, GPT2Tokenizer

model = GPT2LMHeadModel.from_pretrained('gpt2')
tokenizer = GPT2Tokenizer.from_pretrained('gpt2')

# Generate text
inputs = tokenizer("Once upon a time", return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_length=50)
text = tokenizer.decode(outputs[0])
```

### 2. LLaMA (Meta)
```
Open-source GPT alternative

Sizes: 7B, 13B, 33B, 65B parameters

Innovations:
✓ Efficient training
✓ RoPE positional embeddings
✓ Better tokenization
✓ Competitive with GPT-3

Use: Open-source LLM applications
```

### 3. Mistral 7B
```
Small but powerful (7B params)

Features:
✓ Grouped-query attention
✓ Sliding window attention
✓ Beats LLaMA 13B!

Use: Efficient deployment
```

### 4. CodeLLaMA / StarCoder
```
GPT-style models trained on code

Use: Code generation, completion
```

sections.title: T5: Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer
sections.body:
### Architecture: Encoder-Decoder

```
Everything is text-to-text!

Task: Translation
  Input:  "translate English to French: The cat"
  Output: "Le chat"

Task: Summarization
  Input:  "summarize: [long article]"
  Output: "[summary]"

Task: Classification
  Input:  "cola sentence: The cat sat"
  Output: "acceptable"  (text, not label!)
```

### Key Innovation: **Unified Framework**

```
All NLP tasks as text generation:
• Translation: English → French
• Summarization: Long → Short
• Classification: Text → Label (as text)
• QA: Question + Context → Answer
• NER: Text → Tagged text
```

### Model Sizes:

```
T5-small:  60M params
T5-base:   220M params
T5-large:  770M params
T5-3B:     3B params
T5-11B:    11B params
```

### Pre-training: C4 Dataset
```
Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus (C4)
• 750GB of text
• Web scraping + filtering
• Span corruption objective
```

### When to Use T5:
```
✓ Multitask learning
✓ Translation
✓ Summarization
✓ Question Answering (generative)
✓ Any seq2seq task
```

sections.title: FLAN-T5: Instruction-Tuned T5
sections.body:
```
T5 + Instruction Tuning

Training:
  Input:  "Translate this to Spanish: Hello"
  Output: "Hola"
  
  Input:  "Summarize: [long text]"
  Output: "[summary]"

Result: Better zero-shot performance!

Models:
  • FLAN-T5-small (80M)
  • FLAN-T5-base (250M)
  • FLAN-T5-large (780M)
  • FLAN-T5-XL (3B)
  • FLAN-T5-XXL (11B)
```

sections.title: Model Comparison
sections.body:
| Model | Type | Size | Best For | Open? |
|-------|------|------|----------|-------|
| **BERT-base** | Encoder | 110M | Classification, NER | ✓ |
| **RoBERTa** | Encoder | 125M | Better BERT | ✓ |
| **DistilBERT** | Encoder | 66M | Fast inference | ✓ |
| **GPT-2** | Decoder | 1.5B | Generation | ✓ |
| **GPT-3** | Decoder | 175B | Few-shot learning | ✗ (API) |
| **LLaMA** | Decoder | 7-65B | Open GPT alternative | ✓ |
| **Mistral** | Decoder | 7B | Efficient LLM | ✓ |
| **T5** | Enc-Dec | 11B | Seq2seq tasks | ✓ |
| **FLAN-T5** | Enc-Dec | 11B | Instruction-following | ✓ |

sections.title: How to Choose?
sections.body:
### Decision Tree:

```
Need to generate text?
├─ YES → GPT family
│   ├─ Need open-source? → LLaMA / Mistral
│   ├─ Need chat? → GPT-3.5/4 (API)
│   └─ Budget-friendly? → GPT-2
└─ NO
    ├─ Seq2seq task? (translation, summarization)
    │   └─ YES → T5 / FLAN-T5
    └─ Understanding task? (classification, NER)
        └─ YES → BERT family
            ├─ Need speed? → DistilBERT
            ├─ Need best? → RoBERTa
            └─ Memory-constrained? → ALBERT
```

sections.title: Using Models with HuggingFace
sections.body:
### BERT Example:

```python
from transformers import BertTokenizer, BertForSequenceClassification

# Load model
model = BertForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased')
tokenizer = BertTokenizer.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased')

# Encode input
inputs = tokenizer("The movie was great!", return_tensors="pt")

# Forward pass
outputs = model(**inputs)
logits = outputs.logits
```

### GPT-2 Example:

```python
from transformers import GPT2LMHeadModel, GPT2Tokenizer

model = GPT2LMHeadModel.from_pretrained('gpt2')
tokenizer = GPT2Tokenizer.from_pretrained('gpt2')

# Generate
inputs = tokenizer("Hello, my name is", return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_length=30)
text = tokenizer.decode(outputs[0])
```

### T5 Example:

```python
from transformers import T5Tokenizer, T5ForConditionalGeneration

model = T5ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained('t5-small')
tokenizer = T5Tokenizer.from_pretrained('t5-small')

# Translate
input_text = "translate English to French: The cat sat on the mat"
inputs = tokenizer(input_text, return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model.generate(**inputs)
translation = tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True)
```

sections.title: Summary
sections.body:
### BERT Family:
```
✓ Bidirectional encoder
✓ Best for understanding tasks
✓ Masked language modeling
✓ Models: BERT, RoBERTa, DistilBERT, ALBERT
```

### GPT Family:
```
✓ Autoregressive decoder
✓ Best for generation tasks
✓ Language modeling objective
✓ Models: GPT-2, GPT-3, LLaMA, Mistral
```

### T5 Family:
```
✓ Encoder-decoder
✓ Text-to-text framework
✓ Best for seq2seq tasks
✓ Models: T5, FLAN-T5, BART
```
